display.purpose: Signed-out and signed-in app title only.

body.purpose: All other text; system font stack, no webfont loaded.

shadows.name: hover-lift
shadows.purpose: Applied to the two home-screen action cards on hover only; nothing carries a shadow at rest.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: Default shadcn solid button, now resolving to the brand terracotta rather than a per-screen green override.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { background: #b55600; color: #ffffff; padding: 8px 16px; height: 40px; border-radius: 6px; font-size: 14px; font-weight: 500; border: none; transition: background-color 0.15s ease; } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background: #a14400; } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #b55600; outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Outline Button
components.description: Brand-colored outline variant, used for the 'View History' CTA — same terracotta token as the primary button, not an independent color.
components.css: .ds-btn-outline { background: transparent; color: #b55600; border: 1px solid #b55600; padding: 8px 32px; height: 44px; border-radius: 6px; font-size: 14px; font-weight: 500; transition: background-color 0.15s ease; } .ds-btn-outline:hover { background: rgba(181,86,0,0.1); }

components.name: Confidence Badge
components.description: Rounded-full status pill for identification confidence, tiered success/warning/destructive by percentage. Replaces the old green-500/yellow-500/red-500 raw utility classes.
components.css: .ds-badge-success { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; background: #137738; color: #ffffff; border-radius: 9999px; padding: 4px 12px; font-size: 12px; font-weight: 600; }

components.name: Action Card
components.description: Home-screen entry point card (Take Photo / Upload Image) — both cards intentionally share the same terracotta icon-badge treatment (The One Meaning Rule), not color-coded differently.

components.css: .ds-action-card { background: #ffffff; border: 1px solid #e2ddd9; border-radius: 8px; padding: 32px; text-align: center; cursor: pointer; transition: box-shadow 0.15s ease; } .ds-action-card:hover { box-shadow: 0 10px 15px -3px rgb(0 0 0 / 0.1); } .ds-icon-badge { width: 64px; height: 64px; margin: 0 auto 16px; border-radius: 9999px; background: rgba(181,86,0,0.1); display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; font-size: 28px; transition: background-color 0.15s ease; } .ds-action-card:hover .ds-icon-badge { background: rgba(181,86,0,0.15); } .ds-card-title { font-size: 24px; font-weight: 600; color: #1d140d; margin-bottom: 8px; } .ds-card-body { font-size: 16px; color: #6f6763; }

components.name: Care Tip Card
components.description: Three-column semantic-tinted card grid (Watering/info, Light/warning, Soil/success) on the plant result page. Only the heading is tinted; body copy stays plain ink to avoid a low-contrast tinted-on-tinted risk.

narrative.overview: Plant Tracker feels plain, functional, and a little worn-in — something you'd actually carry outside while pointing a phone at a leaf. A single warm terracotta (oklch 0.56 0.15 54 — clay pots, dried botanical ink, sun-baked ground) is the only color the interface asserts on purpose; everything else is a pure-white canvas and a warm-tinted neutral scale built from the same hue. This deliberately sidesteps both the generic AI-green plant-app cliché and the SaaS-cream/parchment default: the warmth lives in the primary color and the icon badges, not in the page background, which stays true white exactly per the 'mood lives in the brand color, not the surface' rule. A second color, a deep ink-navy (oklch 0.28 0.07 235 — fountain-pen ink on a ledger page), exists solely as the info semantic role, used only for the Watering care-tip card. This replaces the previous baseline, which ran on shadcn's unmodified defaults plus ad hoc Tailwind green-600/blue-600 swatches and a green-50-to-blue-50 gradient background.
keyCharacteristics: One committed brand color (terracotta primary) on a pure-white field, per the Restrained color strategy that's the product-register default
Warm-tinted neutrals (chroma 0.006–0.02 toward hue 54) replace shadcn's cold blue-gray 'slate' scale throughout
A standardized 3-state semantic vocabulary (success / warning / destructive) replaces the old ad hoc green-500/yellow-500/red-500/purple-600/orange-600 rainbow
Flat surfaces at rest; shadow-lg appears only on card hover (unchanged from baseline)
Full OKLCH token system in both light and dark mode, verified for ≥4.5:1 text contrast on every filled swatch

rules.name: The Mood-Lives-In-Primary Rule
rules.body: Body background is pure white (chroma 0) in every state, always. Warmth and personality come from primary, icon badges, and typography — never from tinting the canvas cream, sand, or parchment. If a future pass wants more color presence, spend it on primary's usage frequency, not on desaturating the background.

rules.name: The One Meaning Rule
rules.body: Every instance of primary means the same thing: 'the action that moves you toward an identification.' Camera and Upload entry cards on the home screen intentionally share the same terracotta rather than being color-coded differently — an earlier draft tried camera=primary/upload=info, but that invented a distinction with no real semantic weight. Reserve info for its one real job (the Watering tip) until a second meaning actually earns it.

rules.name: The Verified-Contrast Rule
rules.body: Every filled semantic/brand swatch (primary, destructive, success, warning, info) carries white text/icons and was tuned in OKLCH so that white-on-fill contrast clears 4.5:1 in both light and dark mode — not assumed, computed. Warm hues (orange, gold) especially tend to read brighter than their OKLCH lightness suggests, and white text can fail even when the 'L 0.42–0.78 → white text' heuristic says it should work.

rules.name: The Flat-at-Rest Rule
rules.body: Nothing carries a shadow until the user's cursor or touch says otherwise. Kept unchanged from baseline — it already fit the calm, unfussy field-notebook feel.

dos: Do keep body background pure white in every state — the field-notebook warmth comes from primary usage, not canvas tint (The Mood-Lives-In-Primary Rule).
Do verify any new filled color's white-text contrast computationally, not by eye — warm hues are deceptive (The Verified-Contrast Rule).
Do keep primary meaning one thing across the app; resist color-coding entry points or categories unless the distinction is real (The One Meaning Rule).
Do keep the flat-at-rest, lift-on-hover shadow behavior.
donts: Don't let this read as a corporate SaaS dashboard — no sidebar nav, no dense stat-tile grids treated as a KPI board, no boxy enterprise chrome. The 'Your Plant Journey' stat row is a personal-recap moment, not a metrics panel — keep it small and keep every number the same primary color, not a rainbow.

Don't reintroduce raw Tailwind palette classes (green-600, blue-50, purple-600, etc.) — every color in the UI should resolve through a token (primary, success, warning, destructive, info, or a neutral).
Don't add uppercase tracked eyebrow labels or numbered section markers — nothing about a personal plant log calls for landing-page scaffolding.

Don't treat this colorize pass as having finished the typography or layout work — the type scale is still the unexamined Tailwind default and the taxonomy chart's mobile font sizes are off-ramp literals worth a look in a future audit pass.
